html:
The Lambakannas were a Sinhalese clan whose kings ruled Sri Lanka from Anuradhapura for much of its history. On the 900 map they hold the island under the second Lambakanna line, which ruled from the late 600s to 1017.

That line began with Manavanna, a prince who lived in exile at the Pallava court in south India and won the throne with Pallava troops. His heirs built monasteries and great reservoirs and kept close ties with south India, sometimes as allies and sometimes as enemies of the Pandyas and Cholas.

The end came from the Chola Empire. Rajaraja I took the north of the island around 993, and his son completed the conquest in 1017, capturing King Mahinda V. Anuradhapura was abandoned, and when Sinhalese rule returned it was centred at Polonnaruwa. See also Sinhalese kingdoms.
